purpose: Bounded organization/site access record tracing a primary-care shortage designation toward a named service route while preserving the open person-level booking and care stages.

events.geography: Allen County and Lima, Ohio; North Lima Community Health Center
events.date_precision: current source snapshot date; administrative records and patient-facing pages have different publication clocks
events.denominator: One named Ohio HPSA organization and one linked active service site; no patient or appointment denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from HRSA administrative files and official Health Partners of Western Ohio patient-facing pages
events.missingness: No person-level appointment, travel, wait, insurance adjudication, completed care, treatment continuity, health, household time/money, trust, or exit record is retained
events.exposure: A designated primary-care shortage organization is linked to an active named site with 72 listed weekly hours, while site schedule fields are unknown
events.alternatives_before_action: The public route identifies phone and portal options and organization-level same-day, insurance, sliding-fee, and payment-plan policies; it does not show a patient-specific alternative provider or completed booking
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Nominal service presence and a public contact route are visible; overlapping hour displays, inconsistent listed phone numbers, login-gated booking, unknown wait times, a limited/non-substitutive same-day policy, and proof-of-income requirements for continuing a discount create unresolved access friction
events.choice_or_response: The organization directs patients to call the location or use the portal; its general email form does not schedule appointments. The medical page reports limited same-day appointments at each location but says Health Partners does not fill in for another community provider when that provider is unavailable
events.person_or_actor_with_control: HRSA controls designation and site-record publication; the organization controls scheduling, phone/portal routing, insurance handling, and payment-plan implementation; the patient-level outcome is unobserved
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The public system and provider expose a named site, listed hours, services, contact route, organization-level affordability/new-patient policies, and a cost page with discounted and non-discounted medical estimates plus income-documentation rules
events.immediate_outcome: The chain advances from shortage designation to organization identity, named active site, nominal hours, patient-facing services, and a phone/portal handoff
events.protected_outcome: A potential care route and organization-level affordability policy are publicly visible
events.sacrificed_outcome: Usable appointment access, schedule clarity, wait-time visibility, and completed care remain unverified; any health, work, or household burden is unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: Patients carry call, portal, waiting, travel, paperwork, and insurance-verification effort unless the organization absorbs it; the record cannot measure that transfer
events.later_outcome: No later person-level care, continuity, health, or household recovery endpoint is public in this route
events.meaning_and_attribution: The record supports an administrative-access interpretation but contains no patient-reported trust, dignity, blame, or meaning measure
events.public_or_collective_response: Provider policy and public contact routes are observed; patient use, switching, complaint, or political action is not observed
events.counterexample: An active provider with listed hours, affordability policies, limited same-day appointments, and published price estimates can coexist with unknown discount take-up, site-specific booking, wait, fallback, insurance, and completed-use stages
events.source_and_uncertainty: HRSA HPSA and service-site records plus official HPWO pages linked in the retained named-site access record; administrative and provider statements are not person-level utilization evidence

arrows.evidence: The HRSA HPSA row names Health Partners of Western Ohio, organization ID 0516380, in Allen County
arrows.counterexample: A designation is not a person-level unmet-care or usable-access measure
arrows.remaining_gap: Patient need, attempted access, and completed care

arrows.evidence: The HRSA service-site record shares organization ID 0516380 and lists North Lima Community Health Center as active and permanent
arrows.counterexample: An active site is not proof of an available appointment
arrows.remaining_gap: Site-specific scheduling, wait, insurance handling, and completed use

arrows.from: active site with listed hours and provider policy
arrows.evidence: The provider page lists services and phone contact; the contact page directs appointment requests to the location or login-gated patient portal
arrows.counterexample: A contact route can exist without a visible slot, reconciled phone, or completed booking
arrows.remaining_gap: Phone reconciliation, public slot visibility, wait, and appointment completion

arrows.to: completed care and later health or household recovery
arrows.evidence: No person-level appointment, care, or later outcome record is retained
arrows.counterexample: Nominal capacity and organization policy do not establish usable care or recovery
arrows.remaining_gap: Patient insurance, appointment, wait, travel, completed care, continuity, health, work, household burden, trust, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger closes an administrative and patient-facing route from shortage designation to named site and contact handoff. It does not estimate access, utilization, care adequacy, or recovery.
storage_boundary: No patient, appointment, portal, or clinical data is retained; only bounded public administrative/provider fields and explicit open stages are represented.
